koans.about: The scriptures say every being has Buddha nature, so the question seems to answer itself, and Zhaozhou’s *mu* refuses that answer. Later teachers made the word a meditation in itself: the student holds it without taking it as “no” or as “nothing.”

versions.t: 問狗子還有佛性否。師云有。僧云。和尚還有否。師云。我無。僧云。一切眾生皆有佛性。和尚因何獨無。師云。我非一切眾生。
versions.note: The question is already here, but it is put to Weikuan (died 817), not Zhaozhou, and his answer is yes.

versions.t: 上堂，舉：「僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』僧云：『一切眾生皆有佛性，狗子為什麼却無？』州云：『為伊有業識在。』」師云：「大眾！爾諸人尋常作麼生會？老僧尋常只舉無字便休。
versions.note: The first dated version with Zhaozhou. The answer is *mu*, and he gives a reason. Wuzu tells his students he only ever raises the word 無.

versions.t: 只如僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：有。僧云：既有，為什麼撞入這皮袋？州云：為伊知而故犯。又僧問：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：無。僧云：一切眾生皆有佛性，狗子為什麼無？州云：為伊有業識在。
versions.note: Two monks, two answers: yes, because the dog knew, and did it anyway; *mu*, because it has karmic consciousness.

versions.t: 趙州和尚因僧問。狗子還有佛性。也無。州云無。
versions.note: Wumen keeps only the question and the no.

koans.en: The Cypress Tree in the Courtyard
koans.about: To ask the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west, Bodhidharma bringing Zen from India, is to ask what Zen is. Zhaozhou points at the tree in front of them, and the answer is usually read as turning the monk from an abstract question to what is right there.

versions.t: 問：「如何是祖師西來意？」師云：「亭前柏樹子。」僧云：「和尚莫將境示人。」師云：「我不將境示人。」僧云：「如何是祖師西來意？」師云：「亭前柏樹子。」
versions.note: The monk objects, Zhaozhou denies it, and the question and answer come round again. The tree stands before a pavilion (亭), not a courtyard (庭).

versions.t: 吉州秋山和尚。僧問。如何是祖師西來意。師曰。杉樹子。
versions.note: Not a version: the same stock question, put to Qiushan, who answers with another tree.

versions.t: 舉僧問趙州：如何是祖師西來意？州云：庭前栢樹子。趙州庭前栢，天下走禪客。
versions.note: A teacher raises the story to comment on it in verse. The objection is gone, the pavilion is now a courtyard, and 柏 is written 栢.

versions.t: 昔有僧問趙州。如何是祖師西來意。答曰庭前栢樹子。又隨而誡之曰。汝若肯我與麼道。我則辜負汝。汝若不肯我與麼道。我則不辜負汝。而昧者勦之。使古人之意不完。為害甚矣。
versions.note: Huihong, the author, says Zhaozhou followed the answer with a warning, and complains that others have cut it.

versions.t: 趙州因僧問。如何是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。
versions.note: Wumen’s version is the bare question and answer.

koans.about: Asked what the Buddha is, Dongshan names something ordinary, three pounds of flax; some commentators say he was weighing flax at the time. Like the cypress tree, it is usually read as a refusal to give a doctrinal answer, pointing at the plain thing at hand.

versions.t: 僧問洞山。如何是佛。洞山云。麻三斤。師聞之乃曰。向南有竹向北有木。
versions.note: Told secondhand, in the life of another master, Shikuan, who comments on it. The words of the exchange are already fixed.

versions.t: 師在洞山會裏，有僧問洞山：如何是佛？　洞山云：麻三斤。爾後眾皆下語，不契洞山。
versions.note: Ya of Fuyan was there. The story is now a test: the monks offer their own words for it.

versions.t: 如僧問趙州：『如何是祖師西來意？』州云：『庭前柏樹子。』這箇忒殺直。又僧問洞山：『如何是佛？』山云：『麻三斤。』又僧問雲門：『如何是佛？』門云：『乾屎橛。』這箇忒殺直。
versions.note: Dahui sets it beside the cypress tree and Yunmen’s dried dung stick as answers that could not be more direct. The exchange has not changed since 1004.

versions.t: 洞山和尚。因僧問。如何是佛。山云。麻三斤。
versions.note: Wumen’s version is the exchange alone.

gloss.趙州和尚因僧問。狗子還有佛性。也無。州云無。: A monk asked Master Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.”
gloss.趙州因僧問。如何是祖師西來意。州云。庭前柏樹子。: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in front of the courtyard.”
gloss.只如僧問趙州：狗子還有佛性也無？州云：有。僧云：既有，為什麼撞入這皮袋？州云：為: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Yes.” The monk said, “If it has, why did it push its way into that skin bag?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it knew, and did it anyway.” Another monk asked, “Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?” Zhaozhou said, “Mu.” The monk said, “All living beings have Buddha nature. Why doesn’t a dog?” Zhaozhou said, “Because it has karmic consciousness.”
gloss.問狗子還有佛性否。師云有。僧云。和尚還有否。師云。我無。僧云。一切眾生皆有佛性。: Asked: “Does a dog have Buddha nature?” The master said, “Yes.” The monk said, “Do you have it?” The master said, “I don’t.” The monk said, “All living beings have Buddha nature. Why don’t you?” The master said, “I am not all living beings.”
gloss.上堂，舉：「僧問趙州：『狗子還有佛性也無？』州云：『無。』僧云：『一切眾生皆有佛: In the hall he raised this: “A monk asked Zhaozhou, ‘Does a dog have Buddha nature or not?’ Zhaozhou said, ‘Mu.’ The monk said, ‘All living beings have Buddha nature. Why doesn’t a dog?’ Zhaozhou said, ‘Because it has karmic consciousness.’” The master said, “Everyone! How do you usually take this? I usually just raise the word *mu* and stop.
gloss.問：「如何是祖師西來意？」師云：「亭前柏樹子。」僧云：「和尚莫將境示人。」師云：: Asked: “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” The master said, “The cypress tree in front of the pavilion.” The monk said, “Master, don’t teach me with an object.” The master said, “I’m not teaching you with an object.” The monk said, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” The master said, “The cypress tree in front of the pavilion.”
gloss.舉僧問趙州：如何是祖師西來意？州云：庭前栢樹子。趙州庭前栢，天下走禪客。: He raised this: a monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in front of the courtyard.” Zhaozhou’s cypress in the courtyard / sets Chan travelers walking all over the world.
gloss.昔有僧問趙州。如何是祖師西來意。答曰庭前栢樹子。又隨而誡之曰。汝若肯我與麼道。我: Once a monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” He answered, “The cypress tree in front of the courtyard.” Then he warned him: “If you accept what I say, I have failed you. If you don’t accept what I say, I have not failed you.” But the muddled cut this off, so the old master’s meaning is incomplete. It does great harm.
gloss.吉州秋山和尚。僧問。如何是祖師西來意。師曰。杉樹子。: Master Qiushan of Jizhou. A monk asked, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” The master said, “A fir tree.”
gloss.僧問洞山。如何是佛。洞山云。麻三斤。師聞之乃曰。向南有竹向北有木。: A monk asked Dongshan, “What is the Buddha?” Dongshan said, “Three pounds of flax.” When the master heard of it, he said, “To the south there is bamboo, to the north there are trees.”
gloss.師在洞山會裏，有僧問洞山：如何是佛？ 洞山云：麻三斤。爾後眾皆下語，不契洞山。: When the master was in Dongshan’s assembly, a monk asked Dongshan, “What is the Buddha?” Dongshan said, “Three pounds of flax.” Afterward everyone offered their own words for it, and none of them fit Dongshan.
gloss.如僧問趙州：『如何是祖師西來意？』州云：『庭前柏樹子。』這箇忒殺直。又僧問洞山：: A monk asked Zhaozhou, “What is the meaning of the patriarch’s coming from the west?” Zhaozhou said, “The cypress tree in front of the courtyard.” This is direct to the extreme. Another monk asked Dongshan, “What is the Buddha?” Dongshan said, “Three pounds of flax.” Another asked Yunmen, “What is the Buddha?” Yunmen said, “A dried dung stick.” This is direct to the extreme.
gloss.洞山和尚。因僧問。如何是佛。山云。麻三斤。: A monk asked Master Dongshan, “What is the Buddha?” Dongshan said, “Three pounds of flax.”
